about: Facts about the retained model-16 audiodev.o ioctl handlers, read BY EYE from the llvm-objdump disassembly of audioctl_device_ioctl and i2c_device_ioctl (sha256 14c202fa...9bd2). Not produced by anchor_extract.py or anchor_crosscheck.py: it is the third, hand-made reading the runner compares the committed anchor facts against. Numbers and symbol names only; no instruction bytes. Each case lists the external functions its code reaches and the payload words it touches directly through the stack frame (a lower bound: a payload reached through a pointer in a register is not seen), excluding the shared copy-out tail. 'reading' is the plain-language trace; it is a description of the code, not a statement of what the command means.

6.reading: loads payload word 0, a negative value becomes 0, a value above 256 becomes 256, stores it back, then calls eden_set_pwm or dsp_device_set_pwm depending on two fields of sys_mdp

59.reading: passes the address of the payload to populate_time_formats and returns it through the copy-out tail

62.reading: passes the caller's own pointer and the size field straight to audioctl_get_button_state; it never uses the stack copy

63.reading: copies a word from the driver's private state (audioctlpriv+0xac) into payload word 0

64.reading: copies payload word 0 into the driver's private state (audioctlpriv+0xac): the write half of the pair with 63

144.reading: tests bits of payload word 0, sets a port pin through m8260_port_set on one of two paths, then calls audioctl_set_leds with the word

155.reading: moves the payload's first 8 bytes to a global (a string-move through the address taken at offset 0, which the direct-access list cannot see), tests bit 0 of payload word 2, and calls audioctl_ledtimer when it is clear

i2c.reading: li 3, 0 ; blr: returns 0 for every command and reads none of its arguments
